10080.question_text: The murmurings of the congregation in the wilderness against Moses and Aaron were an indication of the people's
10080.explanation:
The Israelites murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness because they doubted their leadership and, ultimately, God’s ability to provide for them.

In Exodus 16:2-3 (RSV):
"And the whole congregation of the people of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness, and said to them, ‘Would that we had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the fleshpots and ate bread to the full; for you have brought us out into this wilderness to kill this whole assembly with hunger.’”

This shows their lack of faith in Moses and Aaron as God’s chosen leaders and in God’s provision for them.

options.text: fear of dying by the sword
inability to get to the promise land

10087.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
10087.question_text: The last event that boosted Gideon's courage to go against the Midianites was the
10087.explanation:
The final event that gave Gideon the courage to attack the Midianites was when he overheard a Midianite soldier’s dream about a loaf of barley bread tumbling into the Midianite camp and overturning a tent. Another soldier interpreted the dream, saying it symbolized Gideon’s victory over Midian.

This is recorded in Judges 7:13-15 (RSV):
"When Gideon came, behold, a man was telling a dream to his comrade, and he said, ‘Behold, I dreamed a dream; and lo, a cake of barley bread tumbled into the camp of Midian, and came to the tent, and struck it so that it fell, and turned it upside down, so that the tent lay flat.’"

Gideon was strengthened by this confirmation that God had given Midian into his hands.

10143.question_text: The disciples celebrated the passover with Jesus because
10143.explanation:
Jesus ate the meal with His disciples on 14 Nisan (one night earlier than the majority of other Jews would eat the official Passover meal) simply because He would not be alive to eat it the following night. He really did not have a choice to do it at the regular time. Jesus ate the Passover meal with eleven out of twelve of His disciples before being betrayed the following day by judas. 

Matthew 26:17 On the first day of the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Where do you want us to make preparations for you to eat the Passover?”

18 He replied, “Go into the city to a certain man and tell him, ‘The Teacher says: My appointed time is near. I am going to celebrate the Passover with my disciples at your house.’” 19 So the disciples did as Jesus had directed them and prepared the Passover.
